name: Netherlands
summary: Opium Act: List I hard drugs, List II soft drugs. Cannabis is tolerated (≤5 g, coffeeshops). Generic NPS ban (List IA) since July 2025; nitrous on List II since 2023. Drug checking (DIMS) is widely available.

emergency.poisonControlNote: The national poison centre (NVIC) only advises health professionals; the public should call 112 or a GP/out-of-hours doctor (huisartsenpost).

callingForHelp: Ambulance staff are bound by medical confidentiality and police are not normally called for an overdose. No Good Samaritan law, but small personal amounts are rarely prosecuted.
drugChecking: Legal and widespread: the DIMS network (Trimbos Institute) offers anonymous testing at dozens of locations nationwide.

opiumwet.title: Opium Act (Opiumwet), version in force from 17 September 2026

gedoog.title: Rijksoverheid: toleration policy for soft drugs and coffeeshops

hardsoft.title: Rijksoverheid: the law distinguishes hard and soft drugs

lsd.note: List I (hard drug). Possession is a crime (max 1 year for a small own-use amount); small amounts for own use are often only seized.

mushrooms.note: Magic mushrooms are List II (banned since 2008), but truffles (sclerotia) are not covered and are sold legally to adults in smartshops.

dmt.note: List I (hard drug); DMT extracts and ayahuasca are illegal.

mescaline.note: Mescaline itself is List I, but peyote and San Pedro cacti are not listed and are sold legally; extracts are illegal.

dox.note: DOB, DOC and DOM are List I; other analogues are banned through the List IA phenethylamine group (since July 2025).

nbomes.note: 25B-, 25C- and 25I-NBOMe are List I; all other NBOMes are banned through the generic List IA phenethylamine group (since July 2025).

2c-x.note: 2C-B and other common 2C-x are List I; remaining analogues are banned through the List IA phenethylamine group (since July 2025).

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are List I; other 2C-T-x fall under the List IA phenethylamine group.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-MiPT are not on Lists I/II, and tryptamines are not among the List IA generic groups, so they are unscheduled.

cannabis.note: Tolerated: ≤5 g and ≤5 plants usually not prosecuted; coffeeshops sell ≤5 g/day to adults (residents rule, enforced locally). Legal-supply trial in 10 towns.

ketamine.note: Not on the Opium Act lists; prescription-only medicine. Selling it breaches medicines law; possession for own use is not a crime.

dxm.note: Explicitly excluded from the Opium Act, so possessing it is not an offence. Whether DXM cough medicines need a prescription was not verified.

nitrous.note: List II since 1 Jan 2023: possession, sale and import banned except for medical, technical or food use. A small amount for own use is a minor offence.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are List I. Dexamfetamine and methylphenidate for ADHD are available on prescription.

mdma.note: List I (hard drug). Possession is a crime; small amounts for own use are often only seized. Testing via DIMS is legal.

cocaine.note: List I. Possession up to 6 years (1 year for a small own-use amount); dealing up to 8 years, import/export up to 12.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Sale and supply to under-18s are banned, and under-18s may not carry alcohol in public places.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is List I (hard drug). GBL and 1,4-BD are not on the Opium Act lists (industrial chemicals). Sodium oxybate on prescription.

opioids.note: Heroin and other opioids are List I; morphine, oxycodone and fentanyl only on prescription. Heroin-assisted treatment exists.

tramadol.note: Not on the Opium Act lists; prescription-only medicine.

benzodiazepines.note: List II (e.g. diazepam) and prescription-only; possession without prescription is an offence.

maois.note: Prescription-only. Harmala alkaloids/Syrian rue are not listed, but ayahuasca contains DMT (List I).
